sheet-9999997-1.description: Sheet 27 of the January 1915 Sanborn atlas of Hackensack, covering the centre of the Borough of Maywood west of Hackensack, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper right. Maywood Avenue crosses the top of the sheet diagonally; below it a regular grid of Passaic, Pleasant, Park, Grove and Terrace Avenues runs down the sheet, crossed by Elm Avenue and, at the foot, Byrne Avenue. North of Maywood Avenue the sheet shows Oak and Poplar Avenues west of Pleasant, and in the upper right Jersey Avenue with a short unnamed street linking it to Maywood Avenue; east of Terrace Avenue, Garden and Coles run to the right edge. Most blocks are laid out in narrow house lots, many still vacant, with scattered frame dwellings and a few stores (bakery, tailor, plumber, barber, cobbler, grocery). Institutions and works named on the sheet: the Maywood Public School on Grove Avenue, the Dutch Evangelical Lutheran Zion's Church on Pleasant Avenue, the temporary quarters of the Maywood Fire Department near Maywood and Pleasant Avenues, an electric railway waiting room on Maywood Avenue, the M.S.A. Club bowling alley on Grove Avenue, and a garage and repair shop making cement and hollow tile on Passaic Avenue. Hackensack Brook crosses the lower part of the sheet and is marked as the Borough of Maywood limits; the blocks south of it carry Hackensack block numbers (452 to 459). A large area east of Grove Avenue below Elm is open land. A water-facilities and fire-department note for Maywood is printed at the right. The lower right corner holds a separate inset of the Hackensack Golf Club at 50 feet to an inch, which is not part of this annotation.
notes: Printed sheet number 27 of the Hackensack atlas, dated January 1915; the catalog record holds this one sheet under Maywood.
Passaic Avenue is now Passaic Street (West Passaic Street north of Maywood Avenue).
Pleasant Avenue south of Elm is now East Pleasant Avenue and then Hamilton Place at Byrne; north of Maywood Avenue it is West Pleasant Avenue.
Park Avenue south of Elm is now West Anderson Street; Grove Avenue south of Elm is now West Lookout Avenue.
Elm Avenue is now Elm Street, Byrne Avenue is Byrne Street, Garden is Garden Street, Coles is Coles Street.
The street marked 'Not Named' between Maywood and Jersey Avenues is now Parkway.
Oak Avenue is drawn offset at Passaic Avenue, as it still is.
Hackensack Brook is labelled as the Borough of Maywood limits; blocks south of it carry Hackensack block numbers.
Note at the right: Hackensack Water Co. supplies the borough at about 70 lbs pressure; volunteer fire department of thirty men with one hand-drawn hose wagon.

Single sheet 27 of the Hackensack atlas (Jan. 1915), showing Maywood: Maywood Av, Passaic, Pleasant, Park, Grove and Terrace Avs, Oak, Poplar, Jersey, Elm, Garden, Coles and Byrne Avs, a 'Not Named' street (now Parkway), Hackensack Brook (Maywood borough limit). Main map at 100 ft to an inch, drawn turned about 52 degrees (north toward upper right). Part 2: inset of the Hackensack Golf Club at 50 ft to an inch, lower right, with only Central Av drawn; not placed. Catalog box was Lyndhurst; reference refetched around Maywood.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Hackensack Golf Club (clubhouse, locker house, shed) on Central Av, 50 ft to an inch (no street junction; only one side of Central Av drawn and no feature shared with the main map; needs position of the 1915 clubhouse along Central Avenue from another source (an earlier/later atlas sheet or historic aerial)).
